sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: Mem0 is a memory layer for AI assistants and agents. It stores facts from conversations, such as a user's preferences, and finds the relevant ones later so your assistant can give personal, consistent answers across sessions.
sixtySeconds.problem: Language models forget everything between conversations, and stuffing whole chat histories into prompts is slow and expensive. Mem0 extracts the important facts once and retrieves only the ones that matter for each new message.
whoFor: Developers building chatbots and AI assistants
Teams adding personalisation to support or agent apps
Builders using LangGraph or CrewAI who need memory
Anyone prototyping long-term memory for agents
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for a ready-made memory API you can use as a Python or npm library, run as your own server with Docker, or use as a managed cloud service.
requirements: An LLM and embedding model; OpenAI is the default

overview: Mem0 keeps memory at user, session and agent level. You call memory.add() with conversation messages and memory.search() with a query, and it returns the most relevant stored facts. By default it uses OpenAI's gpt-5-mini as the LLM and text-embedding-3-small for embeddings, and it supports many other providers.

There are three ways to use it: the open-source library for testing and prototypes, a self-hosted server started with Docker Compose that adds a dashboard and API keys, and the managed Mem0 Platform. An optional NLP extra adds BM25 keyword matching and entity extraction for hybrid search.

A mem0 CLI manages memories from the terminal, and agent skills teach coding assistants how to integrate Mem0. The project is Apache 2.0 licensed. Benchmark scores in the README are for the managed platform, which includes optimisations not in the open-source library.

steps.title: From the repository's server folder, start the stack and create an admin
Or start it and finish setup in the browser wizard

environment.name: OPENAI_API_KEY
environment.description: Needed for the default OpenAI LLM and embedding model; not needed if you configure another provider.

firstRun.title: Try the CLI
firstRun.code:
npm install -g @mem0/cli
mem0 init
mem0 add "Prefers dark mode and vim keybindings" --user-id alice
mem0 search "What does Alice prefer?" --user-id alice

tutorial.title: Give a chatbot long-term memory in Python
tutorial.useCase: Build a terminal chat that remembers what each user tells it.

steps.title: Create the memory and a client
steps.code:
from openai import OpenAI
from mem0 import Memory

openai_client = OpenAI()
memory = Memory()

steps.title: Search memories before answering
steps.code:
relevant = memory.search(query=message, filters={"user_id": user_id}, top_k=3)
memories_str = "\n".join(f"- {e['memory']}" for e in relevant["results"])

steps.title: Answer with the memories in the system prompt, then save the exchange

tutorial.expected: In later messages, the assistant's answers use facts the user mentioned earlier in the conversation.

troubleshooting.problem: Self-hosted server asks for auth after upgrading
troubleshooting.solution: Set ADMIN_API_KEY, register an admin in the wizard, or use AUTH_DISABLED=true for local development only.

troubleshooting.problem: Keyword or entity search not working

troubleshooting.solution: Set OPENAI_API_KEY or configure another LLM provider.
